An alternative residual model is not the canonical remittance baseline

Report an error

01What does this evidence establish?

A balance-of-payments residual model estimates remittances by assigning an assumed residual discrepancy to them. Such an estimate is an alternative model, not a direct observation or the canonical remittance baseline. The estimate considered here rests on material with no publicly accessible original, so, under this resource's publication rule, neither its value nor its producer is reproduced here.

01What does this evidence establish?02What does it measure?03Who or what does it apply to?04How current is it?05What this evidence does not establish06Original source and verification07Method and verification detail

02What does it measure?

An estimate of 2024 remittances produced by a balance-of-payments residual model, kept separate from the adopted remittance baseline.

03Who or what does it apply to?

Yemen as a whole, as an analytical estimate; not an observed official value

04How current is it?

The estimate refers to 2024. It is a model result rather than an observation and should not be read as describing a later year.

05What this evidence does not establish

A residual-model estimate is not an official or observed national value, and the residual is not a direct observation of informal remittances.

Limits of the measure

Errors in other balance-of-payments components, and the assumption made about errors and omissions, flow into the remittance residual; informal remittances are not directly observed.

06Original source and verification

No public link to the original document is available for this source.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

Balance-of-payments residual model. The underlying material has no publicly accessible original, so this record cannot be verified through this resource.

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How can I verify it?

The material behind this record has no public link to its original document, so no source is listed or linked here and no figure from that material is shown. Read the record as an explanation of method, not as a verifiable figure.

How should this record be read?

Read this evidence within the definition, population or group covered, calculation base where relevant, period, geography and method shown on the page. Before reusing or comparing it, check the source, limitations, evidence date and correction history. If a value or source link is unavailable, the page says so rather than filling the gap by inference. This resource does not host source files; where an original-source link is given, check the publisher’s terms before republishing.
